questions.question: State Mendel's law of independent assortment and explain the dihybrid cross of round-yellow with wrinkled-green peas, showing the 9:3:3:1 ratio.
questions.solution:
**Law of independent assortment:** when two pairs of contrasting characters are considered together, the segregation of one pair is independent of the other pair.

Cross RRYY × rryy: F₁ is all RrYy (round yellow). The F₁ makes four kinds of gametes — RY, Ry, rY, ry — in equal numbers, so the F₁ × F₁ cross has 16 combinations.

Counting the phenotypes: 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green, because each character segregates in a 3:1 ratio and (3:1) × (3:1) = 9:3:3:1 by independent recombination.
questions.knowledgeNote: The 9:3:3:1 ratio fails whenever the two genes are linked — recombinants then fall far below 50% and parental types dominate.

questions.question: What is incomplete dominance? Explain with the snapdragon example and give the F₂ ratio.
questions.solution:
**Incomplete dominance** is the condition in which the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype because neither allele completely masks the other.

In snapdragon (Antirrhinum), red (RR) × white (rr) gives pink (Rr) F₁. Selfing F₁ gives **1 red : 2 pink : 1 white** — the genotypic and phenotypic ratios coincide, which never happens with complete dominance.
questions.knowledgeNote: In codominance (AB blood group) BOTH alleles are expressed together rather than blended — that is the difference from incomplete dominance.

questions.question: State the Hardy–Weinberg principle and derive its equation. In a population, 4% of individuals show a recessive trait — calculate the frequency of heterozygotes.
questions.solution:
**Principle:** in a large, randomly mating population with no mutation, migration or selection, allele frequencies remain constant from generation to generation and the genotype frequencies are given by

**p² + 2pq + q² = 1**, where p + q = 1 (derived by combining the gamete frequencies p and q).

Recessive phenotype frequency = q² = 0.04 → q = 0.2, so p = 0.8.

Heterozygotes = 2pq = 2 × 0.8 × 0.2 = **0.32, i.e. 32% of the population** — carriers are eight times more common than affected individuals.
questions.knowledgeNote: Any of the five conditions being broken means evolution is occurring — the equation is the null model against which change is measured.
